newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans state units investing in futures houses.
newsitem.headline: China bans state units investing in futures houses.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has banned domestic futures brokerages from accepting investment from government and army units, financial institutions and foreign investment firms, the China Securities newspaper said on Tuesday.

In China's first directive governing the sourcing of financing for futures brokerages, the China Securities Regulatory Commission intended to ensure "the healthy development" of their business, the newspaper said.

The circular issued recently stipulated that brokerages were banned from accepting investment from government and Communist Party organisations, from army units from non-state groups and from units under the state budget without approval from the State Council, or cabinet.
They cannot accept investment from financial institutions or from foreign or foreign-funded firms, it said.

In addition, futures brokerages must ensure they have the status of a legal person entity, have shown a profit for the past two years and their accumulated investment in futures brokerages and other institutions must not exceed 50 percent of their net assets, the circular said.
The circular bans the use of bank loans to invest in futures brokerages and the swap of shares as a form of investment among futures brokerages is banned, it said.

The investment of one futures brokerage in other brokerages must not exceed 50 percent of its capital and the brokerages must not raise capital through issue of shares to individuals without approval from the regulatory commission, it said.
Investors that do not meet these regulations must ensure liquidation of their investment and transfer of ownership before April 30, it said.
